learningObjectives: Create TestSteps by dragging Modules into TestCases and describe all three creation methods.
Populate TestSteps with TestStepValues and assign the correct DataType (String, Numeric, Date, Boolean, Password).
Manage TestCase WorkStates (PLANNED, IN_WORK, COMPLETED) and apply them correctly.
Use Test Configuration Parameters (TCP) and reference them with the correct syntax.
Apply ActionModes (Input, Verify, Buffer, WaitOn) to control how Tosca interacts with Controls.
Run TestCases in the ScratchBook for trial execution and debugging.
Build dynamic values using Tosca expressions for dates, math, buffers, and random text.
Create and use Libraries (Reusable TestStepBlocks) and resolve references to build reusable TestCase components.

elements.description: An ordered sequence of TestSteps that defines a complete test scenario. Stored in the TestCases section; references Modules for its steps.
A single action or verification within a TestCase, created by referencing a Module or a specific Control. Each TestStep represents one interaction with the SUT.

A container for organizing TestCases in a hierarchy. Can be nested. Best practice: organize by feature or business process. Inside a TestCase, TestSteps are further grouped using TestStepFolders (e.g., Precondition, Process, Postcondition).

elements.text: A TestCase is a recipe: each TestStep is one instruction ('add flour', 'stir'). The ingredients (Modules/Controls) come from the pantry (Modules section). You follow the steps in order to produce the dish (test result).

elements.caption: TestCaseFolder → TestCase → TestStep hierarchy. A TestCase can also reference Library sequences instead of individual steps.

bulletPoints: TestCases live in the TestCases section; Modules live in the Modules section.
Best practice: rename each TestStep to describe its specific action (e.g., 'Enter Username', 'Click Login').
Best practice: ensure TestSteps follow a chronological, logical sequence.

elements.title: Three ways to add a Module as a TestStep (all achieve the same result):
items: Drag and Drop — drag the Module from the Modules section directly into the TestCase. Most visual and intuitive.
Ctrl+T (Fuzzy Search) — press Ctrl+T inside a TestCase, type part of the module name, select it, press Enter. Fastest keyboard method.
Right-Click → Search and Add TestStep — right-click the TestCase folder, select 'Search and Add TestStep' from the context menu.

bulletPoints: All three methods produce identical results — choose based on your workflow preference.
After creation, always rename the TestStep to reflect its specific action.

WorkStates help teams coordinate: reviewers scan for COMPLETED state to know what's ready.

elements.description: A reusable value defined at TestCase or folder level, referenced across multiple TestSteps. Centralizes test data so changes are made in one place.
To reference a TCP in a TestStep value field, use exactly: {CP[NameOfTheTCP]}
items: Outer curly braces { } are mandatory
CP prefix in square brackets [ ] is mandatory
Parameter name goes inside the square brackets

elements.text: Common wrong formats: CP[Name] (missing braces), {TCP[Name]} (wrong prefix), [CP{Name}] (brackets and braces swapped). Only {CP[NameOfTheTCP]} is valid.

elements.description: Right-click the header row in the TestCase view → select 'Column Chooser' → double-click a column to add it to the view.

bulletPoints: TCP syntax: {CP[NameOfTheTCP]} — memorize this exactly for the exam.
Change the parameter value once → all referencing TestSteps update automatically.
Use TCPs for environment-specific values: base URLs, test user credentials, timeouts.

rows: Enters a value into a Control (types text, selects dropdown option)
Reads a Control's value and compares to expected — fails if mismatch
Reads a Control's value and stores it for later reuse in the same TestCase
Pauses execution until a Control reaches a specified state or value

elements.text: ActionModes are verbs: Input = write, Verify = check, Buffer = copy, WaitOn = wait. The same Control can be used with different verbs in different TestSteps.

bulletPoints: Buffer vs. Verify: Buffer = READ and STORE for later. Verify = READ and COMPARE immediately.
Buffer is essential for capturing dynamic runtime values (e.g., generated order numbers).
WaitOn prevents timing failures — use when a loading indicator or async process must complete first.

elements.description: A representation of a Control (button, text field, label, etc.) selected during scanning. When a Module is dragged into a TestCase, each ModuleAttribute becomes a TestStepValue.
The combination of an ActionMode, a Value, and a DataType for a specific Control inside a TestStep. Tells Tosca exactly what to do with that Control during execution.
Specifies the type of value being entered. The 5 DataTypes are: String, Date, Numeric, Boolean, Password.
items: String — default; plain text
Numeric — use for numbers so that 10 and 10.00 are treated as equal
Date — use for date values
Boolean — use for True/False values
Password — masks the value; use for credentials

elements.text: Always set DataType to Numeric when comparing or verifying number values (prices, quantities). Without it, '10' and '10.00' may not match — causing false test failures.
F9 key: toggles between showing all TestStepValues and showing only those with an action specified. Useful for large TestSteps.

bulletPoints: TestStep = Module placed in TestCase. TestStepValue = the data + ActionMode for each Control in that TestStep.
ActionMode color changes visually confirm which mode is selected.
Use the blue downward arrow (▼) in the Value field to select properties like 'Visible == True'.
DataType Numeric prevents '10' vs '10.00' mismatches — set it whenever comparing prices or counts.

elements.description: A built-in Tosca capability for trial runs of TestSteps and TestCases before final execution. Results are temporary and overwritten with each new ScratchBook run.

elements.title: Two ways to run in the ScratchBook:
items: Select one or more objects and press F6 — runs them immediately in ScratchBook.
Add and arrange objects in the ScratchBook view, then run them — useful for combining steps from different TestCases.

elements.text: ScratchBook results are NOT saved. Each new run overwrites the previous result. Use ScratchBook for debugging only — final execution goes in ExecutionLists.

bulletPoints: F6 = run selected object(s) in ScratchBook.
ScratchBook = debug mode. Results are temporary — not recorded.
Also accessible via: right-click TestCase → 'Run in ScratchBook'.

elements.description: Expressions evaluated at runtime to generate values dynamically — current date, random text, calculated numbers. Written inside curly braces using Tosca's expression language. Syntax: {COMMAND[parameter1][parameter2]...}
To recall a previously buffered value, use: {B[BufferName]}
items: {B[PriceBlueJeans]} — recalls the value stored under that buffer name
Buffer name must match exactly (case-sensitive) the name given when the Buffer was set
XBuffer for dynamic parts: {XB[BufferName]} — reads and buffers only the dynamic portion of a string

elements.description: Perform calculations using static values or Buffer references. Syntax: {MATH[expression]}
items: {MATH[{B[PriceBlueJeans]}*25]} — multiplies buffered price by 25
{MATH[{B[SubTotal]}+10.00]} — adds 10.00 to the SubTotal buffer
Operators supported: + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), / (divide)
Tip: right-click Value field → 'Translate value' to test a MATH expression before running

elements.description: Generate unique random values at runtime to avoid test data collisions.
items: {RND[7]} — 7-digit random integer (max 18 digits)
{RND[100][999]} — random integer between 100 and 999
{RANDOMTEXT[10]} — random 10-character string (letters and numbers, max 1024)
{RANDOMREGEX["^[A-Z][a-z]+[0-9]{4}$"]} — random string matching a regex pattern
FUNCTION: DATE, TIME, DATETIME, DAY, MONTH, YEAR, MONTHFIRST, MONTHLAST
[start]: leave empty [ ] to use today's date as the reference
[offset]: d=days, w=weeks, M=months, y=years, h=hours, m=minutes, s=seconds — e.g. [-3y] = 3 years ago, [+4M] = 4 months ahead
[format]: MM=2-digit month, yyyy=4-digit year, dd=2-digit day, MMM=3-letter month abbreviation
Confirmed exam example: {MONTHLAST[][-3y][MMMyyyy]} = last day of month, 3 years ago, in format Jun2022
Exercise 15 example: {DATE[][+4M][MM]} = expiration month +4 months as 2-digit; {DATE[][+3y][yyyy]} = expiration year +3 years as 4-digit

bulletPoints: Dynamic Values are evaluated fresh at runtime — they are NOT static strings.
Buffer recall syntax: {B[BufferName]} — name must match exactly.
MATH syntax: {MATH[expression]} — can nest Buffer references inside.
Date offset units: d=days, w=weeks, M=months, y=years (capital M = months, lowercase m = minutes).
Confirmed exam question: {MONTHLAST[][-3y][MMMyyyy]} = last day of month, 3 years ago, MMMyyyy format.

elements.description: A folder in the TestCases section containing reusable TestCase sequences. Other TestCases reference Library entries instead of duplicating steps.

elements.text: Libraries are stored in the TestCase section — NOT in the Modules section, NOT in Requirements. This is a confirmed exam question: 'In which section are Libraries used? → TestCase.'

elements.description: An individual TestStep sequence stored inside a Library. Can be dragged from the Library into any TestCase.

When an RTSB is dropped into a TestCase, it appears as a Reference with '_Reference' appended to its name (e.g., 'Precondition_Reference'). It remains linked to the Library — any change in the Library propagates to all TestCases using that reference.
items: Drag RTSB from the Library folder, drop into the TestCase or TestStepFolder.
The dropped block is named [OriginalName]_Reference.
All TestCases using the same RTSB are updated simultaneously when the Library block changes.
Use this when you want a single source of truth (e.g., a shared Login flow).

elements.description: Replaces a Library reference inside a TestCase with an inline copy of the Library's steps — making the TestCase self-contained with no external dependencies.
items: Right-click the RTSB Reference → 'Resolve Reference'.
Icon changes after resolving — the block is no longer linked to the Library.
After resolving, changes to the Library NO LONGER affect this TestCase.
Can be undone with Ctrl+Z ONLY before saving. After saving, the resolve is permanent.
Use when a specific TestCase needs a different version of the standard flow.

elements.text: Library folders are sorted alphabetically automatically. When dragging RTSBs, drag individual folders (containing TestSteps) — not the top-level parent folder.

bulletPoints: Libraries eliminate duplication of common sequences (e.g., login flow) across many TestCases.
RTSB dropped into a TestCase → named [Name]_Reference, stays linked to Library.
Resolve the Reference: link → inline copy. Use for TestCase-specific deviations.
Resolve is reversible with Ctrl+Z until the file is saved — after saving it is permanent.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Use the Libraries — Working with RTSB References

elements.title: Step-by-step: building a TestCase from a Library (Exercise 17 pattern):
items: 1. Create a new TestCaseFolder and a new TestCase inside it.
2. Set the TestCase WorkState to IN_WORK.
3. Create TestStepFolders inside the TestCase (e.g., 'Process').
4. Drag the RTSB 'Precondition' from the Library — place ABOVE the Process folder.
5. Drag the RTSB 'Postcondition' from the Library — place BELOW the Process folder.
6. Drag remaining RTSBs (Order Product, Start Checkout, Checkout Process, etc.) INTO the Process folder.
7. Verify the sequence matches the SUT flow.
8. If a specific block needs customization, right-click it → 'Resolve Reference'.

elements.text: After creating the Library (Exercise 16), the TestStepFolders from the original TestCase become Reusable TestStepBlocks. Library folders are auto-sorted alphabetically.

bulletPoints: Create Library: create a TestStepLibrary in TestCases section, drag existing TestStepFolders into it.
Use Library: drag RTSBs from Library → they become References in the target TestCase.
Customise without affecting others: Resolve the Reference on the specific RTSB.

examPitfalls.title: TCP syntax — exact format required
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The exam presents multiple syntax variants. Common wrong options: CP[NameOfTheTCP], [CP{NameOfTheTCP}], {TCP[NameOfTheTCP]}.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The ONLY correct syntax is {CP[NameOfTheTCP]} — outer curly braces, then CP, then the name in square brackets.

examPitfalls.title: Libraries belong to TestCase section
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Distractors place Libraries in the Module section or Requirements section.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Libraries are in the TestCase section. 'In which section of Tosca are libraries used? → TestCase.' This is a confirmed exam question.

examPitfalls.title: WorkState COMPLETED ≠ Approved
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates confuse COMPLETED (set by the tester to signal readiness for review) with Approved (a 4-Eye status set by the reviewer).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: COMPLETED = tester signals the TestCase is done and ready for review. Approved/Completed (4-Eye) = reviewer has validated it.

examPitfalls.title: Buffer vs. Verify
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions describe 'reading a value from the SUT'. Candidates choose Verify instead of Buffer.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Buffer = READ and STORE. Verify = READ and COMPARE to expected. If the scenario says 'store for later use', the answer is Buffer.

examPitfalls.title: Date expression syntax
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The exam gives 3-4 date expression variants. The format order matters: {MONTHLAST[][-3y][MMMyyyy]} — NOT {MONTHLAST[][-3y-1d][mmmyyyyy]}.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Memorise: {MONTHLAST/MONTHFIRST[start-date][offset][format]}. Format MMMyyyy = 3-letter month abbreviation + 4-digit year.

examPitfalls.title: Three TestStep creation methods
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask for all valid methods. Candidates forget right-click → 'Search and Add TestStep'.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Three methods: (1) Drag-and-drop Module into TestCase. (2) Ctrl+T fuzzy search. (3) Right-click TestCase folder → 'Search and Add TestStep'.

examPitfalls.title: DataType Numeric vs. String for numbers
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates leave DataType as String when entering prices or quantities. '10' and '10.00' will not match as Strings.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set DataType to Numeric whenever a value is a number that needs comparison. Tosca then treats 10, 10.00, and 10.0 as equal. Check Settings → TBox → Number formats if verification still fails.

examPitfalls.title: ScratchBook results are temporary
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates think ScratchBook runs are recorded like ExecutionList runs. They are not.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ScratchBook = debug/trial mode only. Results are temporary and overwritten on every new run. For recorded results, use ExecutionLists.

examPitfalls.title: ScratchBook run methods — F6, not F5
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The exam offers F5 as a distractor. F5 does not run in ScratchBook.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: F6 = run selected object(s) in ScratchBook. Two valid methods: (1) select + F6, (2) add objects to ScratchBook and run from there.

examPitfalls.title: Buffer name must be exact
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates recall a buffer using a slightly different name. Tosca will not find the stored value.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Buffer names are case-sensitive. The name in {B[BufferName]} must match exactly the name given when the Buffer ActionMode was set.

examPitfalls.title: RTSB Reference naming (_Reference suffix)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates expect the dragged RTSB to keep its original name. It is renamed with '_Reference' appended.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When you drag an RTSB from a Library into a TestCase, it appears as [OriginalName]_Reference. It remains linked to the Library until 'Resolve Reference' is applied.

examPitfalls.title: Resolve Reference is irreversible after saving
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates resolve a reference thinking they can undo later. After saving, the unlink is permanent.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Resolve Reference can be undone with Ctrl+Z ONLY before saving. Once saved, the TestCase is permanently unlinked from the Library block.

examPitfalls.title: 'Translate value' fails with 'Buffer not found' — buffers are runtime-only
examPitfalls.trapDescription: When testing a MATH/Buffer expression like {MATH[{B[SubTotal]}+10.00+{B[Discount]}]} with the right-click 'Translate value' option, Tosca throws 'Translation failed — Buffer X was not found'. Candidates assume the TestCase is broken.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Buffers are populated only at RUNTIME, when the Buffer ActionMode step executes. 'Translate value' evaluates at DESIGN time using whatever buffers already exist in the current Tosca session — so a buffer set later in the TestCase is 'not found'. Fix: run the TestCase (or the buffering steps) in the ScratchBook (F6) first to fill the buffers, then translate/run. Also confirm the buffer name matches exactly (case-sensitive) and that the Buffer step runs BEFORE the step that recalls it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to add a Module as a TestStep inside a TestCase. Which THREE methods can be used?

options.text: Drag the Module from the Modules section and drop it into the TestCase.
Press Ctrl+T inside the TestCase to open the fuzzy search for Module names.
Right-click the TestCase folder and select 'Search and Add TestStep'.
Double-click the Module in the Modules section to auto-add it to the last active TestCase.

practiceQuiz.hint: Three methods are official; one is invented.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The three official methods are: (A) drag-and-drop, (B) Ctrl+T fuzzy search, and (C) right-click → Search and Add TestStep. Double-clicking a Module does not add it to a TestCase. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester has finished building a TestCase and wants to signal to the review team that it is ready for inspection. Which WorkState should be set?
practiceQuiz.hint: Done + ready for review = one specific state.
practiceQuiz.rationale: COMPLETED signals that all work on the TestCase is done and it is ready for review. PLANNED = not started; IN_WORK = still in progress; APPROVED is not a TestCase WorkState (it belongs to the 4-Eye Principle, not TestCase states).

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to reference a Test Configuration Parameter named 'BaseURL' in a TestStep value field. What is the correct syntax?
practiceQuiz.hint: Outer curly braces + CP in square brackets + name in square brackets.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {CP[BaseURL]} is the correct syntax. Outer curly braces are mandatory. CP goes in square brackets followed by the parameter name in square brackets. TCP is not the correct prefix — CP is.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During test execution, a TestStep reads the order confirmation number displayed on the SUT screen and stores it to use in a later verification step. Which ActionMode achieves this?
practiceQuiz.hint: Read from SUT + store for later = one specific ActionMode.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Buffer reads the current value of a Control from the SUT and stores it in a buffer variable for reuse later in the TestCase. Input writes to the SUT. Verify checks against expected. WaitOn pauses for a condition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestCase must enter today's date but formatted so it reads the last day of the current month, 3 years ago, in 'MMMyyyy' format (e.g., Jun2022). Which Dynamic Value expression is correct?
practiceQuiz.hint: MONTHLAST for last day; -3y for 3 years ago; MMMyyyy for the format.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {MONTHLAST[][-3y][MMMyyyy]} is correct: MONTHLAST returns the last day of the month, [] uses the current date as start, [-3y] subtracts 3 years, [MMMyyyy] formats as 3-letter month + 4-digit year. This is a confirmed AS1 exam question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In which section of Tosca Commander are Libraries stored and used?
practiceQuiz.hint: Libraries contain reusable test sequences — not reusable UI models.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Libraries are stored in the TestCase section, not in Modules, ExecutionLists, or Requirements. They contain reusable TestCase sequences (e.g., a login flow) that other TestCases can reference. This is a confirmed AS1 exam question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester needs to customize the columns displayed in the TestCase view to show additional data columns. What is the correct procedure?

options.text: Go to Tools → Settings → TestCase Columns.
Columns are fixed and cannot be customized in Tosca Commander.
Right-click on the header row and select 'Column Chooser', then double-click to add the desired column.
Drag columns from the Modules section into the TestCase header row.

practiceQuiz.rationale: To customize TestCase columns: right-click the header row → 'Column Chooser' → double-click the desired column to add it to the view. This is the standard Tosca Commander column customization workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test step needs to pause execution until a loading spinner disappears from the page. Which ActionMode is designed for this purpose?
practiceQuiz.hint: It literally means 'wait until the condition is met'.
practiceQuiz.rationale: WaitOn pauses test execution until a Control reaches a specified state or value. It is specifically designed for handling timing and synchronization issues such as waiting for loading indicators to disappear.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After importing a Library reference into a TestCase, the tester wants the TestCase to be self-contained with no external dependencies. What action should they perform?

options.text: Use 'Resolve the Reference' to replace the Library link with an inline copy of its steps.
Export the Library as a Subset and re-import it.
Delete the Library — the TestCase keeps a local copy automatically.
Libraries always remain linked; self-contained copies are not possible.

practiceQuiz.hint: Resolve = replace the link with actual content.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Resolve the Reference' replaces the Library reference with an inline copy of the Library's TestSteps inside the TestCase, making it completely self-contained with no external Library dependency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Once all work on a TestCase is done and ready for review, to which Status should the TestCase WorkState be set?
practiceQuiz.hint: The state that signals the tester is finished and the TestCase awaits review.
practiceQuiz.rationale: COMPLETED is the WorkState that signals the TestCase is finished and ready for a reviewer. 'Ready' and 'Done' are not Tosca WorkState values. IN_WORK = still being built; PLANNED = not started.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You can use a TCP to add values for identifiers of various test environments. This statement is…
practiceQuiz.hint: TCPs are designed for exactly this purpose.
practiceQuiz.rationale: True. Test Configuration Parameters (TCPs) are used to centralize environment-specific values such as base URLs, browser settings, and credentials, so they can be changed in one place and apply to all referencing TestSteps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What options are available if you want to run a test in the ScratchBook? (2 correct answers)

options.text: You can run your objects by selecting them and pressing F6.
You can add and arrange objects in the ScratchBook and then run them.
You need to compile the objects and then run the compiled objects.
The objects will open the necessary locations you need for testing on the SUT, then you fill in the data.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two legitimate ways to use ScratchBook — one keyboard shortcut, one drag-based.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Select objects + F6 (A) and add/arrange objects in ScratchBook then run (B) are the two valid methods. Compilation (C) is not a Tosca ScratchBook concept. ScratchBook is fully automated — the tester does NOT fill in data during the run (D is false). No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements correctly describe TestStep best practices in Tricentis Tosca?

options.text: Rename each TestStep to clearly describe the action it performs.
Ensure TestSteps are structured in chronological order.
Keep all TestSteps generic and unnnamed to maximize reuse.
Always place verification steps before the action steps they verify.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two are documented best practices; two are anti-patterns.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Rename TestSteps to reflect their action (A) and keep them in chronological order (B) are documented Tosca best practices. Leaving steps unnamed (C) is an anti-pattern. Verification steps come AFTER the corresponding action step (D is incorrect). No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester enters the value '10.00' to verify a price field, but the test fails even though the SUT displays '10'. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The ActionMode is set to Input instead of Verify.
The Value field must use the Buffer syntax {B[price]}.
The DataType is set to String — Tosca cannot match '10.00' with '10' as strings.
The TestCase WorkState is PLANNED and cannot execute.

practiceQuiz.hint: A DataType controls whether Tosca treats values numerically or as text.
practiceQuiz.rationale: With DataType String, '10' and '10.00' are different character sequences. Setting DataType to Numeric lets Tosca recognize them as equivalent. Check Settings → TBox → Number formats if issues persist after changing DataType.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester buffers the price of an item as 'ItemPrice' and then wants to verify the total by multiplying the price by 3 and adding 5.00 shipping. Which expression is correct?
practiceQuiz.hint: Buffer recall syntax must be wrapped inside MATH.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {MATH[{B[ItemPrice]}*3+5.00]} is correct: the MATH function wraps the expression, and the buffered value is referenced with {B[BufferName]} inside it. 'ItemPrice' alone (A) is not a valid reference. {B[...]} cannot perform arithmetic (C). {CP[...]} is for Test Configuration Parameters, not Buffers (D).

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test needs a random 10-character string (letters and numbers) entered as a cardholder name at runtime. Which expression generates this?
practiceQuiz.rationale: {RANDOMTEXT[10]} generates a 10-character random string of letters and numbers. {RND[10]} generates a 10-digit random INTEGER (numbers only). {DATE...} is for date expressions. {B[...]} recalls a stored buffer value — not a random generator.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester drags the RTSB named 'Login Flow' from a Library into a TestCase. What name will it appear as inside the TestCase?
practiceQuiz.hint: A suffix is automatically added to indicate it is still linked to the Library.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When an RTSB is dragged from a Library into a TestCase, Tosca renames it as [OriginalName]_Reference — in this case 'Login Flow_Reference'. This naming makes it immediately clear that the block is linked to the Library.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester resolves the reference for one RTSB in a TestCase and then modifies it. Later, the Library block is updated. What happens to the resolved block?

options.text: The resolved block also updates automatically — it is still linked.
The resolved block is unlinked; Library updates do NOT affect it.
The TestCase throws an error because the Library no longer matches.
The resolved block is deleted and must be re-added from the Library.

practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Resolve the Reference' unlinks the block from the Library. Any subsequent Library updates will NOT propagate to the resolved block — it is now an independent inline copy. This is exactly why Resolve is used: to allow TestCase-specific customization without affecting the shared Library.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which expression generates a dynamic expiration date that is 4 months from today, displayed as a 2-digit month?
practiceQuiz.hint: Capital M = Months in the offset. MM in format = 2-digit month.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {DATE[][+4M][MM]} is correct: DATE for a specific date, empty start [] = today, [+4M] = plus 4 months (capital M), [MM] = 2-digit month format. Lowercase m in offset is minutes (B is wrong). MONTH is a date expression output, not a function with offset (C). Option D is missing the + sign and uses %M which is 1-digit format (D is wrong).
